_note: A REGISTER of token vesting, lock and emission contracts, read directly from Ethereum. The unit is a CONTRACT and its current state, not an event on a date. That is the whole difference between this and an unlock calendar: a calendar can only show supply that has a future date attached, and the largest single position here — 45.59% of ENS supply — has no future date at all, because it finished vesting in November 2025 and nobody has moved it. 'Already unlocked and not withdrawn' is a finding, not an absence.
_method: Address established from the project's own primary source (repository, docs or governance record) where one exists, then confirmed on-chain: the contract must return a coherent schedule AND its token() / uni() getter must point at the token it claims to vest. An address that fails either on-chain test is recorded under `unverified` instead, because 'there is nothing readable here' is itself a result. Where no primary source names the address and it was identified by reading the chain, the row carries an `addressNote` saying so — a weaker provenance claim, stated rather than hidden. Every figure below is read at ONE block by scripts/probe-vesting.mjs, whose four-byte selectors are derived with keccak256 and self-tested against published vectors rather than remembered.

states.label: Releasing now
states.meaning: The contract is paying out at a rate it publishes on-chain, and it holds enough to keep doing so. This is the only state a conventional unlock calendar can represent.

states.label: Unlocked, not withdrawn
states.meaning: The schedule has finished and the tokens are still sitting in the contract. Every one of them is withdrawable today, on no notice and with no announcement. There is no date to put in a calendar, so calendars show nothing here.

states.label: Rate published, nothing behind it
states.meaning: The contract publishes a forward emission rate but holds no balance to pay it. Read the rate alone and you forecast supply that cannot arrive.

states.label: Finished and emptied
states.meaning: Schedule complete and the balance is zero — confirmed by reading the balance, not assumed from the date having passed. The distinction between this and 'unlocked, not withdrawn' is invisible without an on-chain read, and it is the difference between nothing and 45% of a supply.

tokens.name: Ethereum Name Service
tokens.addressNote: The address is NOT taken from a document. ENS's own docs name the token but not this contract, so it was identified by reading the chain: it exposes token(), unlockBegin(), unlockCliff() and unlockEnd(), its token() returns the ENS token, and it holds 45.59% of ENS supply. That combination cannot be coincidental, and every step of it is reproducible with an RPC endpoint — but the provenance of the ADDRESS is on-chain inference, not a primary source, and that is a weaker claim than the other rows here make.

schedules.label: DAO treasury lock
schedules.note: The contract publishes the schedule but not the amount originally locked — there is no getter for it — so the figure here is the balance it holds right now, read at the stated block. The four-year linear unlock finished on 4 November 2025, which means all of it is unlocked and none of it has moved.

schedules.label: pre-CRV liquidity providers
schedules.note: The one-year escrow for liquidity providers who were active before CRV existed finished on 13 August 2021. Five years later the contract still holds 10,302,751 CRV of the 151,515,152 it was funded with — claimable by their recipients at any moment, with nothing scheduled and nothing to announce. This row did not exist until the register started reading balances rather than dates.

tokens.name: Uniswap
tokens.note: All four vesters point at the same recipient, 0x1a9c8182c09f50c8318d769245bea52c32be35bc. Their schedules were already on file; what was NOT on file was whether the tokens had actually left, because the data recorded dates and not balances. All four read zero: 430,000,000 UNI, vested and withdrawn. That is the honest opposite of the ENS row, and neither could be told from the other without reading the chain.

unverified.label: Curve — Community Funds
unverified.reason: Holds 845,144 CRV and implements none of the VestingEscrow getters. It is an address with a balance, not a schedule: nothing about a release date is readable from it. The balance is real and the timing is unknowable, which is a different statement from either 'no unlock' or 'an unlock on some date'.

unverified.label: Curve — Investors 1
unverified.reason: Labelled as an investor allocation and exposes no schedule to read. Its balance is now zero, so whatever it held has already moved — but with no getters there is no way to say when, or under what terms.

unverified.label: Lido TRP — per-recipient escrows
unverified.reason: The factory and the prototype are both readable, and the prototype returns a coherent (empty) schedule, so the interface is right. But each recipient's schedule lives in a separate clone whose address only appears in a factory event. Enumerating them needs eth_getLogs over a wide block range, and free RPC endpoints cap that at 50 blocks — about ten minutes of chain. The data exists on-chain and is out of reach at this cost level.

provenanceScale.label: Contract-verified
provenanceScale.meaning: Read from the contract by eth_call at the stated block. Reproducible by anyone with an RPC endpoint.

provenanceScale.label: Project-published
provenanceScale.meaning: From the project's own repository, docs or governance record. Authoritative but not independently checkable on-chain.

provenanceScale.label: Aggregator-sourced
provenanceScale.meaning: From a third-party dataset. Fastest to assemble and the weakest evidence: if a date slips, nothing in the data says so.

emissions.name: Aave Safety Module
emissions.mechanism: emissionPerSecond, fixed until governance changes it
emissions.note: This is NOT new issuance. AAVE's supply is capped at 16,000,000 and fully minted; these tokens move out of the Ecosystem Reserve to stakers, so they are supply arriving on the market rather than supply being created. DISTRIBUTION_END is set to 2123, which is a sentinel meaning 'no end', so the real limit is not the date — it is the allowance the Reserve has granted the staking contract, which is read here too and covers roughly 39 days at the current rate. That number is the honest forward horizon and no calendar publishes it.
emissions.detail: The contract publishes an emissionPerSecond that is constant until governance votes to change it, so the daily figure is exact rather than projected.

emissions.name: Curve DAO
emissions.note: Emission is algorithmic: the contract mints at a fixed rate that steps down once per 365-day epoch. Unlike discretionary vesting, the forward number is readable today.
emissions.mechanism: rate(), stepping down once per 365-day epoch
emissions.detail: rate() returns tokens per second and is held constant until the current 365-day epoch ends and steps down on-chain.

emissions.name: Compound Reservoir
emissions.mechanism: dripRate() per block, paid only out of the balance the contract holds
emissions.note: The clearest case on this page for why a published rate is not a forecast. dripRate() returns 0.5 COMP per block — about 3,600 a day — and has done since block 10,229,427. The contract's own arithmetic therefore says 7,764,561 COMP should have reached the Comptroller by now, and dripped() says 4,504,950 actually has. The difference, 3,259,611 COMP or 32.6% of total supply, is what the contract owes on paper. Its balance is zero, so none of it can move. Anything that reads the rate and multiplies by time forecasts supply this contract cannot deliver.
emissions.caveat: This does not say COMP distribution has stopped. Distribution is governed by the Comptroller, which governance can fund by other routes; what is readable here is only that THIS contract publishes a rate it cannot pay.
emissions.detail: Reservoir.drip() transfers min(rate × blocks elapsed − already dripped, its own balance). With a zero balance that minimum is zero regardless of the rate.
